title: A laser beam towards the Milky Way's centre
caption: A laser beam towards the Milky Way's centre, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A laser beam crosses the southern sky towards the centre of the Milky Way in this wide-angle photograph from ESO's Paranal Observatory. ESO Photo Ambassador Yuri Beletsky took it in mid-August 2010, while astronomers were observing the galactic centre with the laser guide star facility on Yepun, a Unit Telescope of the Very Large Telescope.

The laser makes an artificial star 90 kilometres up, in Earth's mesosphere. Its colour is tuned to excite a layer of sodium atoms, thought to be left over from meteorites, which is why it matches sodium street lamps. The glowing spot acts as a reference for the adaptive optics system, which corrects the atmosphere's blurring and gives sharper observations.
That matters for the galactic core, where a supermassive black hole, circled closely by stars, is swallowing gas and dust. Sharper images let researchers monitor that region better.

understand.summary: This is a wide-angle landscape photograph covering about 180 degrees of sky. The source gives no other camera or exposure details.
understand.eye: The camera's exposure brings out the Milky Way's structure more strongly than the eye would see, and the beam looks brighter than it would in person.

explore: The photo covers about 180 degrees of sky. It was selected as Wikimedia Picture of the Year 2010, and was also Astronomy Picture of the Day on 6 September 2010.
alt: A laser beam shooting from a VLT telescope towards the centre of the Milky Way across a wide sweep of sky.
